name: MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR)
authoritative_source: NASA/GSFC/MOLA Team — USGS Astrogeology Science Center
format: PDS3 binary (MSB_INTEGER, 16-bit) — converted to Esri ASCII Grid (.asc) via extraction script
crs: Simple cylindrical (planetocentric), IAU 2000, -180 to 180 longitude, -90 to 90 latitude, Mars radius 3396.0 km
coverage: Gale Crater region: lon 137.0-138.0, lat -5.5 to -4.5 (extracted from global tile MEGT00N090HB covering lon 90-180, lat -44 to 0)
resolution: 128 pixels/degree, ~463 m/pixel at equator (native MOLA resolution)
units: metres (elevation above areoid, i.e. planetary radius minus areoid radius)
processing_steps: Downloaded PDS tile MEGT00N090HB from https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/mgs-m-mola-5-megdr-l3-v1/mgsl_300x/meg128/megt00n090hb.img (123 MB, 5632x11520, 16-bit big-endian)
Extracted 128x128 sub-grid for Gale Crater (cols 6016-6144, rows 576-704)
Converted to Esri ASCII Grid (.asc) with cellsize 1/128 degree
NoData value set to -9999 (no explicit NoData in MOLA; all cells have interpolated values)
limitations: Polar gaps above 87N and below 87S are sparse (few off-nadir tracks, interpolated)
Elevation uncertainty at least ±3 m due to areoid error (±1.8 m) and regional uncertainties
463 m resolution is coarse for rover-scale pathfinding; sub-kilometre features are not resolved
Slope computed from 463 m cells overestimates fine-scale roughness and underestimates steep short slopes
Gaps in source data were filled by interpolation — no explicit NoData cells in this extract
